```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk[["set"]](echo = TRUE)
library(deSolve)
```

## 1. Frequency-Dependent vs. Density-Dependent SIR
Here we compare standard frequency-dependent transmission ($\lambda = \beta I / P$) against density-dependent transmission ($\lambda = \beta I$) on the S-I phase plane.

```{r transmission-scaling}
# Frequency-dependent SIR model (lam = beta * I / P)
SIR_model <- function(t, state, parameters) {
  with(as.list(c(state, parameters)), {
    P <- (S + I + R)
    lam <- parameters['beta'] * I / P
    
    dS <- mu * P - mu * S - lam * S         
    dI <- lam * S - tau * I - mu * I 
    dR <- tau * I - mu * R
    list(c(dS, dI, dR))
  }) 
}

# Initial conditions and baseline parameters
initP <- 999 
initI <- 1 
initR <- 0 
initS <- initP - initI - initR
istate <- c(S = initS, I = initI, R = initR)

parameters <- c(
  mu = (1 / (50 * 52 * 7)),    
  beta = 0.25,              
  tau = 1 / 10            
)

R0 <- parameters['beta'] / (parameters['tau'] + parameters['mu'])

# Simulation time grid (0 to 365 days)
time_start <- 0
time_stop <- 365 
deltat <- 0.1
tps <- seq(time_start, time_stop, by = deltat)

# Solve frequency-dependent model
out <- deSolve::ode(y = istate, times = tps, func = SIR_model, parms = parameters) 
Flu2009 <- as.data.frame(out)

# Phase-plane plot (S vs I)
plot(Flu2009[["S"]], Flu2009[["I"]], type = "l", ylim = c(0, 1000), xlim = c(0, 1000),
     xlab = "Susceptible (S)", ylab = "Infected (I)", main = "Phase Plane: FD vs DD")

# Density-dependent SIR model (lam = beta * I, no division by P)
SIR_model_dd <- function(t, state, parameters) {
  with(as.list(c(state, parameters)), {
    P <- (S + I + R)
    lam <- parameters['beta'] * I
    
    dS <- mu * P - mu * S - lam * S         
    dI <- lam * S - tau * I - mu * I 
    dR <- tau * I - mu * R
    list(c(dS, dI, dR))
  }) 
}

out_dd <- deSolve::ode(y = istate, times = tps, func = SIR_model_dd, parms = parameters) 
Flu2009_dd <- as.data.frame(out_dd)

# Overlay density-dependent trajectory (explodes rapidly because beta isn't scaled by P)
lines(Flu2009_dd[["S"]], Flu2009_dd[["I"]], col = "sandybrown", lwd = 2)
```

## 2. Parameter Sensitivity Template (`++`, `+`, `-`, `--`)
Here we vary `beta` up and down around the baseline (0.25) in the frequency-dependent model to compare epidemic curves.

```{r parameter-variations}
parameters_pp <- c(mu = (1/(50*52*7)), beta = 0.45, tau = 1/10) # ++ (much higher beta)
parameters_p  <- c(mu = (1/(50*52*7)), beta = 0.35, tau = 1/10) # +  (higher beta)
parameters_m  <- c(mu = (1/(50*52*7)), beta = 0.18, tau = 1/10) # -  (lower beta)
parameters_mm <- c(mu = (1/(50*52*7)), beta = 0.12, tau = 1/10) # -- (much lower beta)

out_pp <- deSolve::ode(y = istate, times = tps, func = SIR_model, parms = parameters_pp) 
out_p  <- deSolve::ode(y = istate, times = tps, func = SIR_model, parms = parameters_p) 
out_m  <- deSolve::ode(y = istate, times = tps, func = SIR_model, parms = parameters_m) 
out_mm <- deSolve::ode(y = istate, times = tps, func = SIR_model, parms = parameters_mm) 

# Plot baseline I(t) and overlay all 4 parameter variations
plot(out[, 1], out[, 3], type = "l", lwd = 2, ylim = c(0, 600), 
     xlab = "Time (days)", ylab = "Infected (I)", main = "Effect of Varying Beta")
lines(out_pp[, 1], out_pp[, 3], col = "darkred", lwd = 2)
lines(out_p[, 1],  out_p[, 3],  col = "red", lty = 2)
lines(out_m[, 1],  out_m[, 3],  col = "blue", lty = 2)
lines(out_mm[, 1], out_mm[, 3], col = "darkblue", lwd = 2)
legend("topright", legend = c("beta=0.45", "beta=0.35", "Baseline (0.25)", "beta=0.18", "beta=0.12"),
       col = c("darkred", "red", "black", "blue", "darkblue"), lty = c(1, 2, 1, 2, 1), lwd = 2)
```

## 3. Adding an Intervention (`SIR_model_interventios`)
Because `SIR_model_interventios` was left undefined in the template, here is how you write it—for example, reducing transmission (`beta`) by 50% starting at Day 40 (e.g., social distancing or mask mandate).

```{r interventions}
SIR_model_interventios <- function(t, state, parameters) {
  with(as.list(c(state, parameters)), {
    P <- (S + I + R)
    
    # Reduce transmission by 50% once time t reaches day 40
    beta_eff <- ifelse(t >= 40, beta * 0.5, beta)
    lam <- beta_eff * I / P
    
    dS <- mu * P - mu * S - lam * S         
    dI <- lam * S - tau * I - mu * I 
    dR <- tau * I - mu * R
    list(c(dS, dI, dR))
  }) 
}

# Run intervention on baseline and high-beta (pp) scenarios
out_interventions <- deSolve::ode(y = istate, times = tps, func = SIR_model_interventios, parms = parameters) 
out_interventions_pp <- deSolve::ode(y = istate, times = tps, func = SIR_model_interventios, parms = parameters_pp) 

# Compare baseline without intervention vs. with intervention at Day 40
plot(out[, 1], out[, 3], type = "l", lwd = 2, ylim = c(0, 300),
     xlab = "Time (days)", ylab = "Infected (I)", main = "Impact of Intervention at Day 40")
lines(out_interventions[, 1], out_interventions[, 3], col = "forestgreen", lwd = 2)
abline(v = 40, lty = 2, col = "gray40")
legend("topright", legend = c("No Intervention", "50% Beta Reduction (Day 40)"),
       col = c("black", "forestgreen"), lwd = 2)
```
